summary: The reader is an undergraduate computer scientist who has studied discrete mathematics (integers, modular arithmetic, gcd and primes at the basic level, sets, bijections, binomial coefficients), undergraduate linear algebra (vector spaces, matrices, rank, Gaussian elimination, dot products, norms), the single-variable calculus a CS degree requires (limits, convergence of sequences and series, basic integrals, logarithms and exponentials), algorithms and complexity (big-O together with Omega and Theta, recurrences, schoolbook multiplication, worst-case running time of Turing machines), and binary arithmetic with basic complex numbers. This covers the sources' integer, bit, linear-algebra, limit and asymptotic bookkeeping, but not prime-number density results, tensor products, operator norms and contractions, Gaussian integers, or the quotient-ring and Fourier machinery beyond the existing concepts.

known.name: Modular arithmetic
known.gloss: Arithmetic on integers in which two integers are identified when a fixed modulus m divides their difference, giving the residue classes Z/mZ, with division with remainder and modular inverses where they exist.

known.name: Greatest common divisor and coprimality
known.gloss: The greatest common divisor of two integers is the largest positive integer dividing both and is computed by the Euclidean algorithm, with two integers coprime when this divisor is one and a family of integers pairwise coprime when every two members are coprime.

known.name: Prime number
known.gloss: A prime is a positive integer greater than one whose only positive divisors are one and itself, and every integer greater than one factors uniquely into primes.

known.name: Binary field and exclusive or
known.gloss: The two-element field {0,1} with addition modulo 2, which on bit strings is bitwise exclusive-or, and multiplication equal to bitwise AND.

known.name: Hamming weight
known.gloss: The Hamming weight of a binary vector is its number of coordinates equal to one.

known.name: Two's-complement representation
known.gloss: A signed integer is stored in a fixed number of bits whose leading bit has negative place value, so that negative values are obtained by complementing the bits and adding one.

known.name: Positional notation and binary representation
known.gloss: An integer is written as a sum of digits times powers of a fixed base b, and in base 2 a binary string of length k represents its value with the leftmost bit most significant, with addition propagating carries.

known.name: Dyadic rational
known.gloss: A dyadic rational is a rational number whose denominator is a power of two, equivalently a number with a finite binary expansion.

known.name: Floor and ceiling functions
known.gloss: The floor of a real number x, written floor(x), is the greatest integer not exceeding x, and the ceiling, written ceiling(x), is the least integer not less than x.

known.name: Binomial coefficient
known.gloss: The binomial coefficient C(n,k) is the number of k-element subsets of an n-element set.

known.name: Finite sets, subsets and intersections
known.gloss: Finite sets with unions, intersections and subsets, where the indicator vector of a subset is the vector with entry one at its elements and zero elsewhere.

known.name: Bijection and permutation
known.gloss: A bijection between two finite sets is a function that is one-to-one and onto, and a permutation of a set is a bijection from the set to itself.

known.name: Cartesian product
known.gloss: The Cartesian product of finite sets is the set of ordered tuples whose i-th entry lies in the i-th set, and it is used to index arrays with several coordinates.

known.name: Lexicographic order
known.gloss: The lexicographic order on tuples compares entries from the first coordinate onward, so the first coordinate is most significant, and row-major order is the lexicographic order of the row and column indices.

known.name: Logarithm and exponential function
known.gloss: The base-2 logarithm log_2 x, also written lg x, and the natural logarithm ln x are inverse to the powers of 2 and of e, and the exponential function exp(x) = e^x is the inverse of ln.

known.name: Limits
known.gloss: The limit of a sequence or of a function is the value its terms or outputs approach as the index or input grows without bound or approaches a given point, written lim.

known.name: Convergence of sequences and series
known.gloss: A sequence converges to a limit when its terms eventually stay arbitrarily close to it, and an infinite series converges when its sequence of partial sums converges.

known.name: Basic integrals
known.gloss: The definite integral of a continuous function over an interval is the limit of its Riemann sums, and for elementary functions it is computed by finding an antiderivative and applying the fundamental theorem of calculus.

known.name: Geometric series
known.gloss: The geometric series a^0 + a^1 + ... + a^k equals (a^(k+1) - 1)/(a - 1) when a is not equal to one.

known.name: Big-Omega, big-Theta and little-o notation
known.gloss: f is Omega(g) when f is at least a constant times g for large inputs, Theta(g) when f is both O(g) and Omega(g), and o(g) when the ratio f/g tends to zero.

known.name: Worst-case running time of a Turing machine
known.gloss: The worst-case running time of a Turing machine on inputs of length n is the maximum, over all inputs of length n, of the number of steps taken before it halts.

known.name: Recurrence relation
known.gloss: A recurrence relation defines each term of a sequence in terms of earlier terms, such as T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n, and is solved by unrolling it or by substitution.

known.name: Schoolbook multiplication
known.gloss: Schoolbook multiplication multiplies two n-digit integers by forming all digit products and adding them with carries, using order n squared digit operations.

known.name: Directed graph
known.gloss: A directed graph consists of vertices and edges, each edge having a tail vertex and a head vertex, and a network of wires and gates forms such a graph.

known.name: Vector space, subspace, basis and dimension
known.gloss: A vector space over a field such as R, C or F_2 is a set closed under addition and scalar multiplication, a subspace is a subset that is itself a vector space, a basis is a linearly independent spanning set, and the dimension is the number of vectors in a basis.

known.name: Linear map and matrix
known.gloss: A linear map preserves addition and scalar multiplication and is represented by a matrix relative to chosen bases, the matrix being invertible when it has an inverse and its transpose swapping rows and columns.

known.name: Matrix rank
known.gloss: The rank of a matrix is the dimension of its column space, equal to its maximum number of linearly independent columns and to its number of pivots after row reduction.

known.name: Gaussian elimination and triangular matrices
known.gloss: Gaussian elimination reduces a matrix to echelon form by elementary row operations, and a triangular matrix has all entries vanishing on one side of its diagonal.

known.name: Dot product and orthogonal complement
known.gloss: The dot product of two vectors is the sum of products of their corresponding coordinates, and the orthogonal complement of a subspace U is the set of vectors whose dot product with every vector of U is zero.

known.name: Vector norm and maximum norm
known.gloss: A norm assigns each vector a nonnegative length satisfying the triangle inequality, and the maximum norm of a vector is the largest absolute value of its coordinates.

known.name: Complex conjugate, modulus and polar form
aliases: absolute value of a complex number
known.gloss: For a complex number a + ib, its conjugate is a - ib, its modulus is the square root of a^2 + b^2, and Euler's formula writes a number of modulus r and argument theta as r(cos theta + i sin theta) = r e^(i theta).
